# Plan Result

## Epic

`epics/epic-01-report-matches-payouts/`. Goal: the expense report totals equal what was actually paid out. Scope: one story, in `src/report.js` only. No implementation was done, because this is a planning run.

**Why the report is high** (`src/report.js:11-17`): `build()` groups `store.all()` by category and never looks at `expense.status`. It therefore adds up rejected expenses, which were never paid and are not on the bank statement. It also adds up `submitted` expenses, which have not been decided yet.

Your finance team is right that the individual expenses are correct. The report over-counts because it includes the wrong ones. I ruled out two other causes:
- **Cache:** every write path calls `invalidate()`.
- **Summing:** `sumCents` is plain integer addition.

No existing test rejects an expense, which is why nothing caught this. I could not confirm the $2,400 figure, because the repo has no data. The planned red test reproduces the mechanism, and finance can re-run the real month after the fix.

## Stories

1. `story-01-01-report-counts-only-paid` *(FAST)*: the report totals only expenses that were paid out. It is a single `story.md` with five Given/When/Then criteria. It also has a red-test-first plan and `npm test` as its command.

## First Story To Run

`story-01-01-report-counts-only-paid`, but only after the assumption below is confirmed.

## Generated Files

- `epics/epic-01-report-matches-payouts/index.md`
- `epics/epic-01-report-matches-payouts/story-01-01-report-counts-only-paid/story.md`

`ai-flow doctor` reports no numbering or story-link problems. Its one warning is that the project docs are still the installed templates. That was already the case and is unrelated to this change.

## Assumptions

- Assumption (unconfirmed): "paid out" means `approved` only, so `submitted` (undecided) expenses are also excluded from the report. The other plausible reading is that only `rejected` ones are excluded, since a pending expense is still a commitment. Question for finance: should pending expenses appear in the category totals? Recommended: no, approved only. If most of the $2,400 is pending expenses, this answer decides whether the fix closes the gap.

## Risks

- The two readings above give different totals, so the answer decides whether the report matches the bank statement.
- Which status literal to use is recorded as a decision for the story. The `'approved'` string is currently owned by `src/approvals.js`.

## Clarification Readiness

Not ready. The blocker is the `submitted` reading above. This was a non-interactive run, so I did not pick the answer myself. Excluding rejected expenses holds under either reading.

## Recommended Next Command

Answer the question on pending expenses (reply "approved only" to accept the recommendation). Then use `/flow-run` for `epics/epic-01-report-matches-payouts/story-01-01-report-counts-only-paid`.
